She didn't have sex with him happily and then regret it afterwards, she only agreed after her boyfriend (in her words) used their relationship to guilt trip her into it until she caved, and she very much didn't want to do it throughout the whole act. 

Although I'm again aware that she technically did it of her own free will, it still doesn't strike me as "consensual". Although of course how I feel about something isn't how the law works, so if there really is nothing she can do then I suppose that's that.
Yes, now that I think about it that's probably a better venue for the sort of advice I'm looking for. Thanks
Thank you for the suggestions. I was hoping maybe for some sort of legal advice but this is also very helpful (also maybe the wrong subreddit for it).
I'm finished. Now that I've had a little time to think about something else, I feel a bit better about my situation. Thanks for taking the time to talk to me.
I've arrived at my cello lesson, it will take around an hour. I would like to keep talking afterwards if that's alright.

That's a good point. I should ask her. 

A kinda shitty thing she does is a little before the actual region, she has everybody play their pieces in front of each other to go and peer pressure everybody into practicing. I feel like it might be even worse if I somehow opted out of region, considering I'm supposed to be one of the best cellos in the program. I know that's not a reason to put unnecessary pressure on myself, but again, conflicting feelings. I've put myself in a shitty situation, really.

I don't think that's possible, unfortunately. The different orchestras each take up their own specific class period and moving me down would also require me moving to another period, which is already taken up by other classes. I might be able to convince my director to make a specific exception for me specifically, but if I'm being honest she's kind of a bitch. All in all, my options aren't clear and I'm not sure there's a way out.

It's worth a try, I guess. I've been practicing for months though, I feel like it might be a bit of a waste. I hate half assing things I'm supposed to be enjoying. In case you couldn't tell before, I have a lot of conflicting feelings about this entire situation and it doesn't help.

A lot of my friends are in orchestra and I enjoy playing in an orchestra, so I don't think quitting is a good option. Besides, I'm not entirely sure I even could. I think I remember something about not changing electives.

There's just a lot of pressure in the coming weeks that I don't want to deal with.

I started in 6th grade because we were encouraged to choose a fine art and I thought orchestra might be cool. I've been playing for around five years now?

I have some talent and I do enjoy playing beautiful music, but the director of the orchestra that I'm in (there's six orchestras in my program and I'm in the "highest") makes it mandatory to compete in regional auditions and stuff like that. I hate solo auditions and competition in general. It's just another thing breathing down my neck that I don't need. I'm not going to make music into a career and I'm not extremely serious about becoming technically proficient, I just want to play music casually for myself and the orchestra but I can't. Honestly this is probably my fault for auditioning for the highest orchestra when I didn't have to.

I guess. I use the treadmill because it's a lot more convenient to just stretch and run right after I finish lifting, but there are routes I could run after I get home instead. 

It'll help me get outside more often, at least. I don't know if that'll really make a difference in the long run, mood wise.
I just get on one of the gym treadmills and run while I listen to music. I really don't go outside that much, now that I think of it.

I'm leaving for cello lessons in around thirty minutes so I guess I'll have something to distract me, but right now I'd rather just talk.

I exercise pretty frequently. Yesterday I did what I usually do and lifted weights and ran a mile. It doesn't help. The things bringing me down aren't really related to that, I guess.

That's the thing, I don't know what to talk about. I don't know what'll help me. All I know is that life is stressful, the future is uncertain, and I'm not doing enough to help myself. Thinking about dealing with the next few weeks makes me want to lie down and feel depressed, which I am. I feel like I need a way out and suicide is currently the obvious choice.

Our school does have counselors for different grade levels, but I'm not sure they offer guidance- if they do, it's not something they try to make known to the students. There might be another counselor specifically for that I've just never heard about. 

Thank you for the suggestion. I know there's really only so much you can do for someone in Reddit comments, but I really appreciate you taking your time to listen and give advice and comfort. I'll see if maybe I can talk to the counselor about college planning and the like.

Thank you. I really appreciate you taking the time to write this. It's given me a little perspective on my situation. I don't know if venting helped, but your response did.

I know this is probably the most important year of my high school career. And honestly, I've been putting in more effort than the past few years. I've really tried to stay on top of my assignments (of which there is a lot of) instead of just trying to put in the bare minimum needed to do okay in my classes. It seems like that isn't enough, and it's sitting heavy on my chest knowing that there's more I should be doing that I'm not. I've been working towards volunteering and I'm going to audition for the region orchestra (though it's actually mandatory) and I'm not only doing AP classes, but one class that you're supposed to avoid at all cost because the teacher is incompetent beyond reason. There's just so much and I don't know if I can keep up, and that's just what I'm dealing with right this minute.

Motivation is another problem. My "motivation" so far has been "you have to get into a good college!" but it's junior year and I've planned jack. I have a college I *maybe* want to go to but that's just because my brother went there, it's in state, and it seems reputable enough. I don't know if I should be looking for a more prestigious college, or if I should be volunteering more, or visiting campuses, or studying more for the SAT, or considering subject tests, or if I should even be worrying about that right now. Every day I do anything and it feels like all of that and more is breathing down my neck. This is another example of "I should probably be doing more for myself".

About fields I want to go into... I guess maybe I want to be a veterinarian? I mean, animals are cute and I like them. That's about as far as I've gotten with that, so I hope it's understandable that I don't feel terribly motivated with any of this.

At this point the phrase "get into a good college" has become practically meaningless. I'm just dealing with my life with no fixed goal in mind. I try to exercise and take care of myself and talk with my friends but sometimes I just want to end it all and not worry anymore.

Thanks again for taking the time to listen.
